method: Direct timestamp inspection of every record in the canonical [0,50000) trace and the fair_v1 disjoint [50000,100000) segment per family; monotonicity checked across the FULL segment (not just first/last row) after correcting a string-vs-numeric comparison bug for small-integer timestamp fields (twemcache).

brightkite.evidence: Raw file (loc-brightkite_totalCheckins.txt.gz) is grouped by user_id first (all of user 0's checkins listed together, in REVERSE chronological order within that user, before user 1 begins) -- confirmed by direct inspection of the first 5 raw lines. Row position has no direct relationship to time.
brightkite.temporal_relationship_to_test: UNKNOWN_INTERLEAVED -- calendar ranges of the canonical and fair_v1 segments overlap almost entirely (both span 2008-2010); the disjoint-by-ROW-POSITION segments are NOT cleanly earlier, later, or non-overlapping in TIME.
brightkite.confidence: HIGH (direct evidence: non-monotonic timestamps within the canonical segment itself, extensive calendar-range overlap between segments)

citibike.evidence: 202401-citibike-tripdata_1.csv is a large multi-station export; row order is non-monotonic in started_at across the full 100,000-row prefix used here (confirmed by direct per-row timestamp check, not assumed).
citibike.temporal_relationship_to_test: UNKNOWN_INTERLEAVED -- nearly identical calendar ranges for both segments (both span essentially all of Jan 1-14, 2024).

wiki2018.evidence: Raw file (wiki2018_pageviews_en.csv) has an empty timestamp column for every row and is sorted ALPHABETICALLY by article name (object_id), e.g. 'en:!!!', 'en:!!!_(album)', ... -- confirmed by direct inspection. This is a static per-article pageview catalog, not a timestamped request log; it has no time axis to reason about at all.
wiki2018.temporal_relationship_to_test: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no temporal dimension exists in this source; the fair_v1 segment is a different alphabetical slice of the same catalog (content-disjoint, but 'future' or 'past' is not a meaningful description).
wiki2018.confidence: HIGH (direct evidence of absence of a time axis)

metakv.evidence: Raw file (kvcache_traces_1_head.csv) header is 'key,op,size,op_count,key_size' -- no timestamp column exists in the source at all (confirmed by direct inspection of the raw CSV header).
metakv.temporal_relationship_to_test: UNKNOWN -- row order may reflect a logged access sequence, but this cannot be independently verified from the available source fields.
metakv.confidence: LOW (absence of evidence, not evidence of absence)

twemcache.evidence: Numeric timestamp field (relative seconds), strictly non-decreasing across all 100,000 rows (verified with correct integer comparison after fixing an initial string-comparison bug); canonical segment ends at timestamp=187, fair_v1 training segment begins at timestamp=187 -- contiguous.
twemcache.temporal_relationship_to_test: LATER (Option D) -- training data is confirmed strictly chronologically after the test period.

metacdn.evidence: Epoch-millisecond timestamp, strictly non-decreasing across all rows; canonical segment ends at 1678864397813, training segment begins 2ms later at 1678864397815 -- contiguous.
metacdn.temporal_relationship_to_test: LATER (Option D) -- confirmed strictly chronologically after the test period.

cloudphysics.evidence: Epoch-microsecond timestamp, strictly non-decreasing across all rows; canonical segment ends at 1577808002637526, training segment begins 31us later at 1577808002637557 -- contiguous.
cloudphysics.temporal_relationship_to_test: LATER (Option D) -- confirmed strictly chronologically after the test period.

summary.conclusion: No single family-agnostic classification holds across all 7 families. The fair_v1 protocol's implicit assumption ('later raw row position = later chronological time') is TRUE and directly confirmed for 3 families, UNVERIFIABLE for 2 families, and FALSE for 2 families (raw order is grouped by entity, not time, with extensive calendar-range overlap between the 'canonical' and 'training' segments). fair_v1 cannot be certified as a uniform, defensible deployment-style temporal protocol across all 7 families as originally framed.
